utterances.text: It is obvious from these decisions that there had been no such system, especially as both municipalities are establishing check-points. But neither Tuzla nor Siroki Brijeg are situated along the border between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia, so they are creating the preconditions in order to levy revenues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, my question is by way of -- are there any similarities between establishing a custom border and what is happening here, where everything that goes in and goes out is being checked and some sort of tax is being levied on it?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: The establishment of a customs administration is a precondition for producing documents which serve as a basis for levying taxes. These check-points are something of a para-customs service doing this kind of work for the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. If we go to the next document, 1D 01400, this is an order imposing a war tax, and if you could look at this very quickly, and please tell us what is this -- comment briefly on this, and what is a war tax?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: A war tax on turnover was introduced, which is in addition to the existing tariff, the rate of which was 10 per cent, and an additional 30 per cent for cigarettes. But bread, flour, fats, et cetera, are exempt. This revenue is for the Municipality of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, and then one more point, very briefly. If we look at Roman numeral VII and Roman numeral VIII, it says that noncompliance in this order will be considered a violation with serious consequences. And then if we look at Roman numeral VIII, it says that the order shall take immediate effect and special inspection organs of the Tuzla Municipal Assembly shall monitor its implementation. Now, looking at this, can you tell us what is meant by "serious consequences," and who are or what is the special inspection organ or organs, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let's talk about economic and financial issues. You've just said that there was a 10 per cent turnover tax. I assume that this tax was levied on those who were selling those goods, but this tax probably had an inflationary effect, because companies probably had to increase their prices by 10 per cent in order to be able to pay it. Wasn't that an effect of this 10 per cent levy, and didn't it cause distortions in competition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, the result of all these municipal decisions was that there was ever less money, because the municipalities sucked out more and more money in terms of taxes; and it was difficult to do business, to purchase goods, et cetera. But, of course, you can't tackle inflation at municipal level. Municipalities are fighting for their survival and to finance their defence. And if you read all these municipal decisions, you will conclude that they were passed by more or less competent people, but for the most part there was a low level of competence and little knowledge about inflation and about the exhaustion of economic operators, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at 1D 01401, this is an order adjusting the work of the pension and disability insurance fund to war conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could give us a brief comment on this, and of course this is 8 July 1992. And was this municipality, for instance -- was it the sort of function that a municipality could undertake on its own?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This is about an order which a municipality has no authority to pass, because the fund of disability and pension insurance of Bosnia-Herzegovina was obliged to adopt its own official document about its activities in wartime conditions and prescribe how the branch -- branches of that institution throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina are to work. Here, the municipality sets forth the rules for Tuzla in order to meet the needs of the Tuzla citizens for the services of the pension fund.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go to the last document dealing with Tuzla, and that's 1D 00836. 1D 00836. This is an order to impose a war tax on net salaries, and if you could give us just a very brief comment on that, on this one. And of course you could look at Roman numeral I and Roman numeral VI in particular, but feel free to look at other parts of this document as well.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This is an example of how those decisions about the imposition of the wartime tax were passed. It was not a single, flat-rate tax. It depended on the salary. But in Article 6, you can see this exhaustion and the confiscation of the financial assets of the businesses, because it says here that once the salaries and contributions to the salaries are paid, all surplus funds are to be transferred to the Tuzla municipality as the beneficiary. So it is impossible for the companies to use those funds to increase their production, to expand and to develop, but any surplus money was to be paid into the Tuzla account because the Tuzla municipality took upon itself the responsibility of procuring various goods and materiel for the purpose of the war, as you can see in Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again if I may ask you very concretely, prior to the conflict, the breakout of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was a municipality such as Tuzla, or any other municipality, capable or were they permitted to carry out such functions, to pass such decisions as this one?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- okay, I won't ask you the next question because it may be calling for speculation. All right. Now, let's -- we're going to turn to another chapter, and this is a period dealing with when the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the HVO HZ-HB, was up and running, you told us that you were appointed on or about the middle of August; and so now let's look at this period in history. And I'm going to start off with 1D 00003. And if you have it in front of you, sir, this is dated, we see, 14 August 1992. This would have been a day, I take it, before your appointment. This is a decree on the establishment of public accounting -- public auditing service. We see it's signed by the president of the HZ-HB, Mate Boban. Could you please give us a very brief comment on this?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a fundamental decree establishing the public auditing or accounting service, and it was on the basis of this decree that other regulations were passed, ensuring the functioning of the SDK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was this necessary at the time, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: It shows that -- how necessary and how crucial the SDK was in the effort to organise life, and this is probably why it was among the first decisions to be passed, although there are no specifics here in -- pursuant to Article 3, the HVO HZ-HB was supposed to regulate those specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go to the next document, 1D 00012, that would be "12," this is a -- of 14 August 1992, this is a conclusion on refusal to accept credit obligations which were accepted by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I believe you did make some reference to what's contained in this conclusion, but can you please look at it and give us a brief comment?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time information started coming in about the government in Sarajevo incurring debts, and this was, in fact, a response to those news, since none of the money that was obtained through those loans reached the HZ-HB, so this is probably a response to the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in Article 1, we see one-third of the resources acquired. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, and the reason why I'm focusing on this one-third is because earlier you had indicated that there were three trucks of that new currency on BiH, and can you tie in that part of your testimony with this particular conclusion?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, pursuant to this conclusion, a request was made every time contacts were made that one-third would always be transferred to the HZ-HB. Here, we are talking about the BH dinars, but I know that the economy department always thought that one-third of the oil, fuel oil, wheat, whatever, be transferred to HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at the next document, 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm looking at this document, and I'm wondering whether this document is not the manifestation by Mr. Mate Boban of his hostility towards the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, since this document seems to be saying that he is refusing the obligations which were accepted by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, credit obligations, that is, and that he doesn't want to have any responsibility whatsoever, in financial or economic terms. What conclusions can be inferred from such a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conclusion is as follows: The areas of HZ-HB, the municipalities that were in the area of the HZ-HB, would not participate in the servicing of those loans if -- unless one-third of the money has come into their area, because when a state takes a loan, it has to repay it from its budget, and the revenues from the budget are collected from the municipalities. And this is one of the problems that we had inherited from the former Yugoslavia, I would say, when it came to the investments made into some areas in the former state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time in August or July, June, August 1992, who was lending money to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Were there international institutions, were there countries, private entities? Who was lending important amounts to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I had a guarantee issued by the Komercijalna Banka, bank from Sarajevo for the Ministry of the Interior. The amount was huge. The guarantee was to the amount of, let's say, 10 million US dollars, and in case of default and the activation of the guarantee, then the debt would have to be repaid from the budget of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; and I am not aware of any other debts that existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the lender in this particular case, this is the Bank of Sarajevo, the Commercial Bank of Sarajevo, did it not ask for guarantees when lending money or did the bank blindly lend $10.000 [as interpreted] without worrying where the money was going, or had they asked for guarantees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically in this case, it was a bank that had the Minister of the Interior among its founders. That was the guarantee that I saw. But the guarantor under this guarantee was the budget of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so if the Ministry of the Interior were unable to repay the debt, then the state would have to repay it. So if the situation normalised, let's say, and if anyone paid -- if everyone were to pay their taxes, then we would not get as much revenue back because those debts would have to be serviced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps a hypothetical may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's just say that the government in Sarajevo or the president of the Presidency were to order a number of satellite phones. Let's just say nine. And the cost would have to be borne, obviously, by Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is what Mate Boban saying here, that those costs should not be borne by Herceg-Bosna unless three of those satellite phones were also provided for their use, for the use in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go on to the next document, 1D 00013, we can see that this is a decision on the establishment of the competence of the Customs Administration in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna during an imminent threat of war or a state of war. That's the title of it. It's dated 28 August 1992, and it's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic. Are you familiar with this document, first of all?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And how are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Because I drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And could you please explain this very briefly for us?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the initial decree establishing the Customs Administration, and here we simply say that all the valid regulations, passed in accordance with the decree of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Official Gazette 2/92, will be in force, and that the finance department will create other conditions for the functioning of the Customs Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... dwelling too much on the preamble, perhaps you could look at that very quickly, because it begins by saying: "Starting from the fact that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina has derogated the federal institutions with its declaration of independence and the fact that due to the state of war, it has not established a customs service in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and with the aim of protecting legal entities and natural persons in foreign transactions, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, pursuant to Article 18 of the statutory decision ..." And it goes on. What is this preamble attempting to state at the beginning, when it talks about the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its declaration of independence and what have you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: It is clear from this that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina has the authority to establish the Customs Administration, because once Bosnia and Herzegovina declared its independence, the Customs Administration of Yugoslavia no longer had any authority in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Concretely, do you know whether the state authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina were ever prevented by anyone, especially those residing in the areas of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, from establishing a customs administration at the borderline between these two countries now?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: None of the organs ever came up with this idea of establishing a customs service and taking control of the border and the border crossings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go to the next document, P 00412, P 00412, dated 28 October 1992, this is a decree on the opening of accounts of the budget of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna during an imminent threat of war. If you could look at this very quickly, and perhaps I should first ask you: Are you familiar with this decree, and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this decree because I took part in drafting it, and this decree indicates the accounts where the revenue of -- revenues should be paid that are meant for the HZ-HB budget. Those accounts should be opened with the SDK Mostar and with the commercial bank. What it meant was that a non-resident account should be opened in a commercial bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document, 1D 00047, here we have instructions on the opening accounts, possession of assets and implementation on the decree of opening deposit accounts of the budget of HZ-HB during an imminent threat of war or state of war. Do you recognise this document, and if so, could you please comment on this very quickly? What does it attempt to do; these instructions, that is?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This instruction now specifies the account number where those monies are to be transferred to public revenues, and it is quite clear from this that for revenues 1 to 3 to 5, those accounts are to be opened in every unit because this revenue should be shared with the municipalities, and other accounts are to be opened only in the central unit in Mostar, where the finance department has its seat. And here we also deal with some technical issues about the organisation of the SDK, what the accounts should look like, the various codes for various municipalities, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we see that it bears your name, so that is you, right, Neven Tomic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a bylaw on instruction that I could pass, because it was put in my powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So this is sort of like an implementing instrument to the previous instrument that we saw, the decree; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00019. This is a decision on the application of Articles 25 to 35 of the Law on Customs, and of course we see the Official Gazette of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Could you please tell us what this decision is about, focusing again on some articles such as 2. We see Bosnia-Herzegovina is being invoked, citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Article 3 and so on. If you could please comment on this very briefly.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: The Law on Customs in the former Yugoslavia, which was adopted by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, stipulated that there should be a special decision on the implementation of customs privileges, exemption from payment of customs. This was a lower level of legislation and it could be changed at that level. You didn't have to go through the Assembly, through the Parliament, with this. So this decision, 25 to 35, as it was known in the business community, defined the exemptions for citizens, institutions, companies and so on. Here you can see in Article 4 that there are exemptions for the armed forces of the HZ-HB and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and for the organs of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and you can see further down that it is a non-discriminatory decision, that it applies to all the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were entitled to those exemptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to kindly ask you to slow down just a little bit. And also when you -- if you're pointing out something in the document, it might be helpful to some of us if you made reference to a particular article. You talked about the armed forces. I suspect you were referring to Article 4, where it says the armed forces of HZ-HB and RBH, the Republic of --

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. All right, thank you. Now, if you look at the next document, 1D 00066, this is -- these are the rules governing procedure for claiming exemption from customs duty. Again, what -- are you familiar with this document? You must be, because it bears your name. And could you please explain, what are these rules?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: These are the rules on the implementation of the 25/35 decision on the exemptions, and it specifies documents that are necessary to claim the exemption in an appropriate procedure before the customs service. So this lists all the elements of the rules that regulated this area -- that used to regulate this area before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at 1D 00020. This is a decision on the flat tax of customs duty and value of goods. If you could please give us a brief commentary. We note that your name is after Article 7, and we also can see, in Article 3, that it makes reference to US dollars.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This decision was there because of the nature of the customs system. There had to be a flat customs rate that existed in the Yugoslav system. And dollars are mentioned here because dollars were used in the previous law instead of the German mark when values were determined for the value of goods that could be transported across the border, imported and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00023, this is a decision on determining goods subject to a special duty to meet taxation requirements, and it goes on. Again, we see your name. Could you please tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, this is yet another para-fiscal rate, which is the result of a former system, the laws that were in force in Yugoslavia and were adopted by Bosnia and Herzegovina. For all intents and purposes, this is a repetition, and this repetition is here only because this was published in the Official Gazette, which was to be distributed, and then people could regulate this because the Official Gazette that regulated this area, dated from 1991 and 1992, the amendments were from 1992; and it was not at the disposal of the businesses and citizens. So together with the customs tariff, you had to also pay the two times 7.5 per cent and 1 per cent for the recording fee, so a total of 16 per cent. This is a fiscal duty. Why? Because it was meant, in Yugoslavia, as a source of revenue for the subsidies to some producers of some goods in Yugoslavia that were supposed to produce goods so that they don't have to be imported anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00026, this is a decree on governing the application of the RBiH decree on the provisional regulation on the turnover tax of goods and services, and it goes on. Could you tell us what this is -- what this decree is about?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This is the implementation of the decree that was passed in early 1992, after the declaration of independence, and practically this is the law that was in force in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time. But I have to say, once again, that because there were no official gazettes, which are important for the functioning of the budget of the economy of the custom service of the tax system, this decree was to be published and adapted to the wartime, to the state of war; so it was provisional in all of its versions, and it was the same as the one that was passed in accordance with the tariff and also not on the other bases, and that's the -- that was the basis for the calculation of customs, duty and tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00027. Here we see a rate scale of turnover tax of goods and services, dated 31 August 1991. And if you could look at this, and of course we do have the benefit at the very end of this document of a statement of reason -- statement of reasons, and of course I'm sure you will assist us in understanding what is a statement of reasons that's attached to this.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the tariff of the rate on the basis of which the rate of the turnover tax is calculated. I've already said that this is a tariff that was taken over from that that was applicable throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. We can see here 65 per cent, or engines and gasoline, Siroki Brijeg, 40 per cent; cigarettes, 90 per cent; and -- well, that's what happened before the war as well, whereas Siroki Brijeg had 40 per cent, I think. So practically this is a document on the basis of which the turnover tax for goods and services would be calculated for the HZ-HB in case of imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00025, this is a decree on the allotment of revenue generated from the turnover tax. If we look at it very quickly, and please tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, we've already seen accounts for all municipalities for the turnover tax of goods and services. The SDK would automatically, depending on the kind of tax involved, send 75 per cent of the turnover tax to the HZ-HB account and 20 per cent to the municipality, from which the payment of the said tax was made. This decree was very important in terms of preparing the municipalities to accept this system and to know that part of the revenues would remain directly in the budget of the said municipalities, and through the budget of the HZ-HB they would also benefit because services would be paid for that particular municipality as well, those that would have to be paid for by the republican budget otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00028, this is the decree on the rate of income tax and contribution. And if we look at Article 2, it talks about a synthetic rate of 80 per cent. Perhaps you could explain to us what this decree is about, and what do you mean by "synthetic rate"?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: In terms of net salaries, taxes and contributions had to be paid. When the state of war came into existence and when funds were no longer there, and they had been financed by revenues, this prescribed a flat rate of 80 per cent of taxes and contributions. On the eve of the war, it was roughly 80 per cent or so, but now it was a flat rate. That is to say, there was no analysis involved in terms of how much would go for higher education, how much for this, how much for that. Rather, 80 per cent would be paid to the budget of the HZ-HB. However, 10 per cent of those resources paid from a particular municipality would be returned to that municipality for the municipal budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00030, this is a decree on the introduction of war tax in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If you could just very briefly discuss this.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC
utterances.text: This is one of the decisions that was supposed to be of assistance in building a united economic space. The municipal decisions relating to 10 per cent, 8 per cent, 20 per cent, all of this involved differences, meaning that companies would move from one municipality to another, thereby creating additional chaos in the field of control and checks. Therefore, a war tax was established that would be imposed throughout the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is better to stop now, since we have two minutes left. And as you know, there is an important hearing at half past 4.00, so we mustn't run late. The Registrar has just told me that you have had three hours and forty-six minutes so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Three hours and how much? Forty-six?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Forty-six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Unfortunately, we're going to have to carry on with some of this tax documentation. Joe the plumber would not be happy, who is being mentioned in the US presidential race. But, in any event, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, as I have told you already, you must not contact the Defence counsel anymore, and we shall see you again tomorrow morning at 9.00. I wish you all a pleasant evening, and see you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
